newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek farmers plan road blocks despite warnings.
newsitem.headline: Greek farmers plan road blocks despite warnings.

text.p: Greek farmers began a new round of protests on Tuesday to press economic demands despite government threats to use force to stop them blocking roads.

A 25-day blockade in December paralysed road traffic and left thousands of trucks stranded along highways. The farmers suspended their action during the Christmas and New Year holidays but vowed to repeat it if demands were not met.

The farmers' protests began with rallies in the northern town of Karditsa and nearby villages. They plan to occupy public buildings across central Greece on Tuesday and on Wednesday to block the main north-south railway.
"We will block public services, tax offices and toll booths in our area to prevent the state from collecting money," farmers' representative Yannis Patakis said.
The protest will climax on February 4 when the farmers plan to use their tractors to block main roads at six key junctions, cutting Greece in half.
"Blocking national roads and the railroad is illegal and the state won't stand back and tolerate criminal acts," Justice Minister Evangelos Yannopoulos told reporters.
Yannopoulos accused Greece's Communist Party (KKE) of being behind the protests and said those who block the roads will be arrested and prosecuted.
"We will answer the state's brutality by offering flowers to riot police. The government wants a civil clash but it won't happen," said George Apostolidis, a cotton grower in Karditsa.
Government officials said riot police units were on standby near Karditsa and the central town of Larissa, headquarters of the farmers' protest.

Farmers are demanding lower fuel costs and cuts in Value Added Tax on farm equipment, higher price supports, especially for cotton, and a $1.3 billion rescheduling of debts to the state Agricultural Bank.
The government has said it can not meet any of the farmers' demands as agriculture policy is set by the European Union.
